title: Height-Balanced Invariant Enforcement in a C# Distributed Task Scheduler: Jobs, Retries, Leases, and Failures
topic: Distributed Task Scheduler System Design: Jobs, Retries, Leases, and Failures
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Distributed task schedulers must reconcile dynamic job admission, lease-based ownership, and failure recovery while preserving deterministic ordering guarantees. We present a height-balanced binary search tree (BST) as the core indexing structure for a C\# scheduler that tracks job metadata, retry counts, and lease expirations. The tree guarantees $O(\log N)$ point and range queries, $O(\log N)$ insertions, and $O(\log N)$ rebalancing, as proven by static abstract syntax tree (AST) inspection and formal invariant proofs. The scheduler's state machine enforces strict height-balance and key-order invariants, ensuring that concurrent lease renewals and failure notifications do not violate ordering semantics. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; all claims are supported by static analysis and formal reasoning. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/csharp-enterprise-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261015_170118_distributed_task_scheduler_sys}
